A video of what you do in a tab, for someone to watch. Record it from a file of commands sent with
pw-repl send --file, not command by command: the time between commands sent one by one is in the video.

1. Set its size first: viewport 1280x720 (help viewport). Then try the flow without recording, and note
the selectors it needs (#id, text=..., role=...), not snapshot refs: the take starts again from a fresh
page, where the refs are stale.

2. Write the take, one command per line, then run it: pw-repl send --file take.txt (pw-repl help,
outside the REPL, has the rest). Its first lines put the page back as it was before the rehearsal (goto
<url>), so the take does not start from the rehearsal's end. A toast, the cursor and highlights stay up
across page loads: turn off any the rehearsal left (toast off, cursor off, highlight off) before record
on.

    goto https://shop.example/support/new
    record on clip.webm
    cursor on #subject
    type #subject Package arrived damaged
    select #area Shipping
    click #send
    wait text Ticket filed
    record off

3. While it records, pw-repl paces it for a viewer (help record): type types at a readable pace (use it,
not fill, for text the viewer should see typed), each action and each highlight is followed by a pause,
an element out of view is scrolled to smoothly, and the video starts and ends on a still page. highlight
<selector> draws a box to point at something, and toast <text> a line of text saying what is happening,
up for as long as the viewer needs to read it. After a step that loads a page, wait for text only the
result shows (wait text ...), not a heading the page always has, and not wait load: a single-page app
loads nothing.

record on --steps also saves when and where each step ran, in seconds into the video and its pixels, for
editing it afterwards.

The user's own screen, with their real pointer, takes a screen recorder they run (OBS, ffmpeg -f
x11grab, macOS screencapture -v): ask first. playwright-cli itself is a separate tool that records a
clean browser of its own (here, its video-start is record on).

  record [on [file] [time] [options] | off [file]]  record the selected tab's page to a video
  cursor [on [<selector> | <x> <y>] | off]          draw a pointer where the REPL acts, for videos
  toast <text> [options] | toast off                show a line of text over the page, to narrate a video
